name: Popover
description: A panel anchored to a trigger, on the platform's own Popover API: the top layer, light dismiss and focus return are the browser's, and the position is CSS anchor positioning.

props.name: trigger
props.description: The trigger, handed the ref and props that wire it to the popover. It has to be a button.

props.name: children
props.description: The panel's content. Rendered whether or not the popover is open — see the note on mounting.

props.name: open
props.description: Controlled open state. Leave it out and the popover owns it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether it starts open, when the popover owns its own state.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Fires with the new state and why it changed — `'trigger'`, `'escape'`, `'outside-pointer'` or `'imperative'`. A close cannot be refused: the browser has already done it by the time this runs.

props.name: label
props.description: The panel's accessible name. `role="dialog"` has none of its own, and a dialog without one is unusable.

props.name: labelledBy
props.description: Names the panel after an element already on the page, instead of `label`.

props.name: side
props.description: Which side of the trigger the panel sits on — `top`/`bottom` are the block axis, `start`/`end` the inline one, so a panel beside its trigger mirrors in a right-to-left page. Default `'bottom'`.

props.name: align
props.description: Which of the trigger's edges to line the panel up with along the other axis. Default `'center'`.

props.name: offset
props.description: The gap between trigger and panel, on the ÷4 spacing scale. Default 2 — 8px.

props.name: flip
props.description: Whether a side with no room may be swapped for its opposite. Default `true`.

props.name: matchWidth
props.description: Whether the panel is at least as wide as its trigger. Default `false` — a panel sizes to its content.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Whether opening moves focus into the panel. Default `true`, which is what APG asks of a dialog. An `autofocus` attribute inside wins: the browser applies it first and this only acts on what is left.

keyboard.action: On the trigger, toggles the panel.
Closes it and returns focus to the trigger, from anywhere inside.
Moves into the panel from the trigger, and out of the panel to whatever follows it.

a11y: `role="dialog"` on the panel, named by `label` or `labelledBy`; the popover attribute supplies no role at all, and a panel with none is announced as a group of orphaned content.
The trigger carries `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-controls`, so the control says what it operates and what state it is in.
Focus moves into the panel on open and back to the trigger on close. Nothing is trapped: this is a non-modal dialog, so Tab leaves it, and the panel follows the trigger in the DOM either way.
